title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter & token/event ordering in streaming framing
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming framing where partial JSON payloads could be delivered with delimiter/token ordering issues causing downstream parsers to see malformed partial JSON. Improves robustness of OpenAI-compat streaming by ensuring delimiter ordering and token/event emission guarantees. Includes tests and a short canary rollout.
description:
Context: We continue to see flaky client-side JSON parse errors in the SSE streaming path when large responses (or aggressive chunking) hit client boundaries. Root cause: the framing code could emit token/event fragments such that the stream delimiter ("

"/event separator) arrived after a token event boundary, which caused some OpenAI-compat clients and partial-JSON reassemblers to observe out-of-order delimiter/token sequences and fail to assemble valid JSON. In addition, some partial-JSON framing code assumed atomic token/event emission which is not true under continuous batching and some kernel-level chunking.

What this PR does: 1) Reorders delimiter emission in the SSE framer so that event delimiters are always flushed before token/event payload chunks when an event boundary is reached. 2) Adds defensive reassembly logic in openai_compat/partial_json_reassembler to tolerate split token metadata (token id/offset) arriving across adjacent chunks and to validate delimiter boundaries explicitly. 3) Adds end-to-end tests that simulate adversarial chunk boundaries (delimiters split, token events split across chunks) and a small integration test against the JS OpenAI-compat client harness. 4) Adds a short canary flow (console flag + telemetry) to roll this out to 10% of streaming traffic for 24h before full rollout.

Implementation notes: - Framer changes (sse/framer.rs): ensure delimiter bytes are written/flush-ordered before emitting any chunk that starts a new JSON partial; make delimiter emission idempotent for retries. - Streamer adaptor (sse/streamer.py): adjust async flush ordering to avoid interleaving when multiple coroutines push chunks concurrently. Introduce a framing mutex for writer order in hot paths (micro benchmark shows <2% latency impact at p95). - OpenAI compat (openai_compat/partial_json_reassembler.py): add deterministic state-machine for partial-json assembly and explicit delimiter detection; add tests to cover token/event ordering permutations. - Tests: unit tests for framer and reassembler, and e2e/integration harness that reproduces the previously observed client error rates.

Testing and validation: - Local unit tests: added 14 tests covering delimiter splits and token splits. - CI integration: e2e streaming tests run in CI with mocked chunking — flaky case reproduced locally and passes after changes. - Canary: rolled to 10% traffic for 24h in us-west, no increase in parse errors and small telemetry shows reduced client-side JSON errors.

Related: references ENG-842 (streaming stability), ENG-859 (openai-compat improvements), and a support ticket SUP-412 reporting customer parse errors.

Checklist:
- [x] framer ordering fix
- [x] reassembler robustness
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] canary rollout flag + telemetry
- [x] changelog/release note entry

Notes: This touches hot code paths in the streaming runtime; I kept locking minimal and measured impact with microbenchmarks. See bench/perf-notes.md for p95 comparisons. If we observe any regression in p99 under Dedicated high-throughput workloads we can fallback the canary and revert the writer-ordering change while keeping the reassembler resiliency.
